programmes.t: Building to the Sky S1 - "Made in America 1885 - 1930"
programmes.d: Emerging from Chicago and New York, early tall buildings like the Chrysler and Empire State set the foundation for the architectural race to the sky.

programmes.t: Xploration Awesome Planet S6 - "Teens Making An Impact"
programmes.d: In this episode, we’ll meet teens that are working to make the planet a better place with innovative ideas and lots of hard work.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S2 - "Student Astronaut Contest"
programmes.d: Join Emily as she gets to know the winner and together, they prepare for space.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S2 - "Mojave air and Space Port"
programmes.d: Join Emily Calandrelli as she explores Mojave Air and Space Port and the technologies of tomorrow that will lead the way in space exploration.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S2 - "Aliens"
programmes.d: Join Host Emily Calandrelli as she explores the latest in science’s search for life outside of planet Earth.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S3 - "Citizen Science"
programmes.d: Host Emily Calandrelli discovers various ways the public is helping scientists explore outer space; from sending bacteria samples to the International Space Station to tweeting observations about the Northern Lights.

programmes.t: Xploration DIY Sci S6 - "Science Of Suds"
programmes.d: Steve Spangler creates crazy ways to make bubbles at the Children’s Museum of Denver at Marsico Campus.

programmes.t: The Re-Inventors S2 - "Panjandrum"
programmes.d: Rockets, 100 pounds os explosives, and a "wheel of fiery death". For the Re-Inventors it's just another day, another danger.

programmes.t: The Re-Inventors S2 - "Windmill"
programmes.d: Over 1000 years old windmill design. Is it still usable today?

programmes.t: The Re-Inventors S2 - "Crematorium"
programmes.d: Crematorium heated by sunlight, find out if the sun can turn a person into a pile of ashes.

programmes.t: The Re-Inventors S2 - "Flame Thower"
programmes.d: A thousand years old Chinese flamethrower, will it be a real weapon or just a kitchen tool for flaming.

programmes.t: The New Frontier S3 - "Living Planet"
programmes.d: With continuous observation of Earth from orbit scientists have built a data set over time that reveals much about how the Earth breaths and life sustains itself on this living Planet.

programmes.t: The New Frontier S3 - "Cosmic collisions"
programmes.d: Cosmic and x rays, these mysterious and highly powerful particles from deep space are being investigated to finally discover where they come from.

programmes.t: The New Frontier S3 - "Gravity"
programmes.d: LISA pathfinder, has led the way for a space-based gravity wave detector, what are gravity waves and why are they so hard to detect?

programmes.t: The New Frontier S3 - "Interface"
programmes.d: The Ionosphere is little understood, it effects radio communications, GPS signals and satellites alike, it changes between day and night and is influenced from space and from Earth, new satellites have been launched to study this zone.

programmes.t: Angry Planet S2 - "Thunder Down Under"
programmes.d: In the first week of December – the height of storm season in Australia, we plan to travel with Jimmy Deguara, the most experienced of Australian stormchasers.

programmes.t: Angry Planet S2 - "Hawaii"
programmes.d: We have filmed extensively in Hawaii, filming big-wave surfing at the famous Banzai Pipeline on Oahu’s North Shore, and filming George surfing with the “Hawaian Fire” firefighters. We have also filmed at the Hawaii Tsunami Institute and in Hilo.

programmes.t: Angry Planet S2 - "Italia Wild"
programmes.d: Italy is one of the very few nations in the world that regularly gets three major extreme natural phenomena – volcanos, flooding, and avalanches. The most recent eruption was in November 2006.

programmes.t: Destruction Decoded S1 - "Tornadoes"
programmes.d: Explore with us the most destructive tornadoes in history, why could no one predict it?

programmes.t: Exceptional Engineering S1 - "Emergency Helicopter"
programmes.d: In Bavaria, engineers build the high-tech H145 rescue helicopter, while skilled pilots navigate extreme terrain to save lives.

programmes.t: Bridging the Expanse S1 - "The Wonder of Bridges"
programmes.d: Pre-industrial societies around the world construct early bridges, reflecting evolving technologies and expanding human exploration.

programmes.t: The World of Bridges S1 - "China"
programmes.d: We visit China's most famous Wind and Rain Bridge and the Ponte dei Salti in the Verzasca Valley that literally dates back to the Roman era.

programmes.t: The World of Bridges S1 - "Wales"
programmes.d: The Millau Viaduct in the south of France is one of the highest bridge structures in the world while the Pontcysyllte Aqueduct, which stands high over the River Dee in northeast Wales, was built in the 19th century.

programmes.t: The Flying Kestrel: The Renovation Diaries
programmes.d: The owner of Kestrel Beer buys an original 1930’s Riley Kestrel, with the intention of restoring it and then breaking the land-speed record. This documentary follows the events from restoration to record day.

programmes.t: Supersonic: The Great Adventure
programmes.d: The epic story of 70 years of supersonic innovation, from Chuck Yeager's breakthrough to the future of flight.

programmes.t: Disruptive Behaviour
programmes.d: Reuben Christian travels to Istanbul to meet the innovators who are changing the city and discover how technology is disrupting the old order.

programmes.t: Breakthrough S1 - "Modern Day Killer Asteroid"
programmes.d: 66 million years ago, an asteroid slammed into Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula, causing a dinosaur mass extinction. With over 700,000 asteroids in space, what's in store for humanity and our planet if it happens again?

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Carbon Sinking"
programmes.d: Massive sargassum blooms are choking beaches, but a Scottish company plans to sink the seaweed to trap carbon and tackle climate change.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Carlo Rovelli A Conversation"
programmes.d: Neil Cairns visits physicist Carlo Rovelli in Verona to explore time, black holes, and the mysteries of quantum physics.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Cooling Cities"
programmes.d: Reya El-Salahi meets Alexander Valentino, who plans to use Naples’ ancient canals and aqueducts to cool the city in summer.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "DNA Archaeology"
programmes.d: Neil Cairns visits archaeologists and geneticists who traced a 20,000-year-old deer tooth pendant to a Stone Age woman.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Saving the Iberian Lynx"
programmes.d: Reya El-Salahi visits Spain’s Sierra Morena to see how conservation brought the Iberian lynx back from under 100 to thriving again.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Imaging the Aurora"
programmes.d: Reya El-Salahi explores how the northern lights can disrupt technology and visits EISCAT 3D, a new radar studying solar particle impacts.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Long COVID"
programmes.d: Emma meets Dr. Asad Khan, whose life was upended by long COVID, as new research seeks answers for millions still suffering worldwide.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Rewilding Bison"
programmes.d: Emma Keeling treks through Romania’s Tarcu Mountains to see how European bison, once extinct in the wild, are making a comeback.

programmes.t: The Chain: How The World Works S1 - "Food"
programmes.d: At the World Food Championships, a $5 burger reveals a massive global chain of space-visible greenhouses, cow rearing, and historic ketchup.

programmes.t: The Chain: How The World Works S1 - "Transport"
programmes.d: At a Formula-E race in Chile, we uncover how tree sap, pink lithium lakes, molten rock, and top-secret paint create cutting-edge electric cars.

programmes.t: The Chain: How The World Works S1 - "Sport"
programmes.d: Inside LA's SoFi Stadium, a touchdown is made possible by Chinese rare earths, plastic grass, specialized ball factories, and fizzy sodas.

programmes.t: The Chain: How The World Works S1 - "Apparel"
programmes.d: At a massive secondhand market in Ghana, the global fashion chain is traced through high-water cotton, stretchy oil denim, and bug-made silk.

programmes.t: The Chain: How The World Works S1 - "Healthcare"
programmes.d: Inside a Boston maternity ward, the complex medical chain reveals how flowers become painkillers and one Pakistani town shapes global surgery.
